I am an old woman, 76 years, and this small maize plot near my house is only a tiny piece — less than one tinad. I cannot buy a whole sack of fertilizer for such a small patch, it is too much money for me, and my hands are not strong like before. I will put the manure from my few animals on it like I always do, and use the seed I saved from last year's harvest — my mother taught me this way and it has fed us. My children and grandchildren help me with the digging and weeding because I am too old to do the heavy work alone.
